predecessors.note: The Olmec centres were abandoned c. 400 BC; the Epi-Olmec page starts this culture c. 300 BCE.

capitals.name: Tres Zapotes
capitals.note: Principal centre, not a political capital. 'By 250 CE, Cerro de las Mesas, Remojadas, and other sites further north along the Veracruz coast had eclipsed Tres Zapotes'. Coordinates from the gazetteer's place entry.

correction.text: central Veracruz and the Papaloapan River basin, around Tres Zapotes, Cerro de las Mesas and La Mojarra

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row): Cliopatria's last Olmec shape (-366..-351, the Tuxtlas around Tres Zapotes) plus a 40 km band along the Papaloapan. The page gives no area or population figure.

region.text: the Papaloapan River basin of central Veracruz

ledger.note: 300 BC: the Epi-Olmec culture succeeds the Olmecs in the Papaloapan basin, 'from roughly 300 BCE to roughly 250 CE'. Tres Zapotes 'continued to be occupied well past 400 BC, but without the hallmarks of the Olmec culture' (Olmecs page). The year is the page's round figure; the land is the researcher's reading of 'the Papaloapan River basin'.

region.text: the Papaloapan basin; Tres Zapotes eclipsed by Cerro de las Mesas and Remojadas

ledger.note: 250: the Epi-Olmec culture gives way to Classic Veracruz. 'By 250 CE, Cerro de las Mesas, Remojadas, and other sites further north along the Veracruz coast had eclipsed Tres Zapotes'; the Classic Veracruz culture page dates its own culture 'from roughly 100 to 1000 CE'. No state follows on this land in the project (the classic-veracruz-culture dossier is the El Tajín polity from 600), so the coast returns to nobody.

sources.title: Epi-Olmec culture
sources.note: Identity, 300 BCE–250 CE, the Papaloapan basin, Tres Zapotes eclipsed by 250 CE.

sources.title: Olmecs
sources.note: Tres Zapotes 'occupied well past 400 BC' without Olmec hallmarks; the predecessor's end c. 400 BC.

sources.title: Classic Veracruz culture
sources.note: The successor culture's date range (100–1000 CE) and extent (Pánuco to Papaloapan).

notes: Written because Cliopatria's Olmec row (-366..-351) is really this culture and the Gulf coast between 300 BCE and 250 CE would otherwise be blank; not named in the group scope, type 'culture' as for the Olmecs. The Classic Veracruz culture page (100–1000 CE, Pánuco to Papaloapan) describes the successor culture; the project's classic-veracruz-culture dossier is the El Tajín polity from 600, so the central Veracruz coast 250–600 stays nobody's land unless a Classic Veracruz culture-type dossier is added.
